# TypeSOL

> Write Solana programs in TypeScript. TypeSOL compiles a TypeScript subset to native SBF (no interpreter, no
> generated Rust) and writes an Anchor-compatible IDL and a typed client for every program. npm: @typesol/cli.

Integers are bigint (1n, u64), everything is imported from "typesol", and there is no throw, async, class or float.
The rules and the whole reference in one file: https://typesol.com/llms-full.txt

## Docs

- [language](https://typesol.com/docs/language/): the language guide: an overview, its pages and where each construct is described
- [language-basics](https://typesol.com/docs/language-basics/): what a program is: instructions, account data, helpers, constants, files
- [language-types](https://typesol.com/docs/language-types/): integers, strings, enums, structs, options and lists, with their bytes and limits
- [language-statements](https://typesol.com/docs/language-statements/): which TypeScript is TypeSOL, functions and closures, and what is refused
- [language-accounts](https://typesol.com/docs/language-accounts/): account parameters, the checks they emit, constraints and account layouts
- [language-pdas](https://typesol.com/docs/language-pdas/): seeds, bumps, signing as a PDA, PDAs in the IDL
- [language-errors-events](https://typesol.com/docs/language-errors-events/): require, error codes, logs, events and return values
- [language-cpi](https://typesol.com/docs/language-cpi/): calling other programs: System, tokens, Metaplex, Stake, invoke, transfer hooks
- [language-chain](https://typesol.com/docs/language-chain/): sysvars, hashes, signatures, introspection, oracles and randomness
- [language-native](https://typesol.com/docs/language-native/): advanced: porting native programs (raw views, Borsh accounts, panics)
- [language-builtins](https://typesol.com/docs/language-builtins/): every name typesol exports, one line each
- [errors](https://typesol.com/docs/errors/): the error codes a program fails with
- [test-your-program](https://typesol.com/docs/test-your-program/): tests with typesol/testing in LiteSVM
- [cli](https://typesol.com/docs/cli/): the typesol commands
- [client](https://typesol.com/docs/client/): the typed client every build writes
- [migrate-from-anchor](https://typesol.com/docs/migrate-from-anchor/): each Anchor construct and its TypeSOL form
- [troubleshooting](https://typesol.com/docs/troubleshooting/): common problems
- [mainnet](https://typesol.com/docs/mainnet/): deploying, verifying and publishing the IDL
- [security-model](https://typesol.com/docs/security-model/): what a compiled program checks for you and what is left to you
- [ai](https://typesol.com/docs/ai/): the agent rules, check --json hints and the MCP server
- [stability](https://typesol.com/docs/stability/): what is stable, what is experimental, the road to 1.0

## Tools

- `npx @typesol/cli init my-app`: a project with a program, a LiteSVM test, AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md and the MCP server configured
- `npx --no-install typesol check --json`: errors with hints; `npx --no-install typesol mcp`: check, IDL and docs as MCP tools

## Optional

- [Case studies](https://typesol.com/docs/case-study-marginfi/): mainnet programs (Marginfi v2, Phoenix v1, SPL Stake Pool, Raydium AMM v4, CLMM, CP-Swap, Jito) ported and checked against their binaries
